title: Romantic Varaždin for Couples: Getaway Guide 2027
metaDescription: Plan a couples' trip to Varaždin, Croatia: baroque Old Town, the park-like cemetery, Trakošćan Castle, wine hills, festivals, costs and practical tips.
content:
## Why Varaždin Works for Couples

Varaždin is a former Croatian capital with a compact baroque centre. Everything a couple needs sits within a 15-minute walk: pastel palaces, a moated castle, green parks and café terraces. Zagreb is 79 km to the south, about 1 hour 15 minutes by car and roughly 2 hours by bus or train. The town is calm, cheap by European standards and rarely crowded outside festival weeks.

## Best Romantic Things to Do in Varaždin

### Walk the Old Town and Its Moat Park
The Old Town (Stari Grad) is a Gothic-Renaissance fortress on the northern edge of the centre. It is separated from the city by embankments and moats. Its walls and towers date mostly from the 14th to 16th centuries. Since 1925 it has housed the Varaždin City Museum. The grounds are free and suit a slow evening walk. The museum is normally open Tuesday to Friday 9:00–17:00 and Saturday and Sunday 9:00–13:00. It is closed on Mondays and public holidays. The castle interior and permanent exhibition were closed for renovation through 2026, so confirm the reopening date with the city tourist board before planning around it.

### Sit on King Tomislav Square
The main square is lined with pastel baroque façades, and the terraces fill up from late afternoon. Order a coffee (€2–3) or a glass of continental white wine (€3–5) and watch the town hall. The square is at its best around sunset, when the façades turn warm and the day-trippers have left.

### Visit Varaždin Cemetery
This is the most unusual couples' stop in the city. The cemetery has been in use since 1773. Landscape architect Herman Haller redesigned it in 1905 as a park, with thousands of thuja trees clipped into geometric shapes, plus birch, maple and magnolia. It is protected as a horticultural monument and belongs to the European Cemeteries Route. Locals use it for walks. Keep voices low, and skip a guided tour: the paths are easy to follow alone, and the atmosphere is better in quiet, with late-afternoon light.

### Visit the Gallery in Sermage Palace
The baroque Sermage Palace holds the Gallery of Old and Contemporary Masters. Its old-masters section covers the 15th to 19th centuries, with a baroque focus that matches the building. It makes a good rainy-day option for two hours.

### Picnic in the Parks
The green belt around the Old Town and the King Tomislav park have shaded paths, benches and small ponds. Buy bread, cheese and local cured meats at the town market and eat outdoors. A picnic for two costs about €10–15.

## Day Trips for Couples from Varaždin

### Trakošćan Castle
Trakošćan is a hilltop castle above an artificial lake, about 40 km from Varaždin. A path circles the lake in roughly 30–40 minutes. Go on a weekday morning to avoid tour groups. Organised day trips from Zagreb that combine it with Varaždin cost roughly €100–125 per person, but a rental car or taxi from Varaždin is cheaper for two.

### Zlatne Gorica Wine Hills
The Zlatne Gorica (Golden Hills) lie on the outskirts of Varaždin. Small family cellars sell white wine and offer simple food in a quiet setting. Reserve by phone or ask the tourist board for current cellar listings, because many open only on set days.

### Varaždinske Toplice
This thermal spa town has Roman roots and appears in a document of 1181. It works as a half-day trip for couples who want a spa afternoon.

## Best Time to Visit Varaždin as a Couple

| Season | What to expect |
|---|---|
| Late May | Gourmet Varaždin and the MOP multimedia festival; mild weather |
| July | Courtyard festival; warm evenings, few tourists |
| Late August | Špancirfest, about 10 days of street performers and music; more than 100,000 visitors |
| September | Varaždin Baroque Evenings, with concerts in churches and theatres |
| October | Flying Guitars festival; quieter streets, autumn colours |

For couples, September beats Špancirfest. The August festival is fun, but accommodation fills, the squares are packed and the baroque calm is lost. Choose Baroque Evenings if you want atmosphere without the crowds.

## Where to Stay in Varaždin
Choose a hotel or apartment near the Old Town or King Tomislav Square. Everything worth seeing is within walking distance, and you will not need a car in town. Mid-range doubles generally cost €70–120 per night outside Špancirfest, and prices rise sharply during the festival. Book at least two months ahead for late August.

## Sample Two-Day Couples Itinerary

**Day 1:** Morning walk through the Old Town grounds. Lunch in the centre. Afternoon at the Sermage Palace gallery. Sunset drink on King Tomislav Square. Dinner of local dishes such as štrukli (baked cheese pastry), which usually costs €6–10 per portion.

**Day 2:** Drive to Trakošćan for the lake walk. Return for a late-afternoon stroll in Varaždin Cemetery. Finish with wine in the Zlatne Gorica hills or in town.

## Local Tips for Couples
- Most museums close on Mondays, so plan cafés, parks and the cemetery for that day.
- The centre is largely pedestrian and bike-friendly. Hiring bikes lets you reach the cemetery and park quickly.
- Restaurants fill on Friday and Saturday evenings, so reserve a table the day before.
- Cards are accepted in most places, but keep a few euros in cash for market stalls and small cellars.

faq.question: Is Varaždin good for a romantic weekend?
faq.answer: Yes. The centre is compact, car-free in parts and full of baroque architecture, parks and café terraces. Two nights cover the Old Town, the cemetery park, King Tomislav Square and a day trip to Trakošćan.

faq.question: How many days do couples need in Varaždin?
faq.answer: Two nights are enough for the town and one day trip. Add a third night if you want a spa afternoon in Varaždinske Toplice or an unhurried visit to the Zlatne Gorica wine hills.

faq.question: What is the best month for a couples' trip to Varaždin?
faq.answer: Late May and September are best, with mild weather and cultural events such as Gourmet Varaždin and the Baroque Evenings. Late August brings Špancirfest, which is lively but crowded and expensive.

faq.question: How far is Varaždin from Zagreb?
faq.answer: Varaždin is 79 km north of Zagreb. The drive takes about 1 hour 15 minutes, and buses and trains take roughly 2 hours.

faq.question: Is Varaždin Cemetery a good place for couples to visit?
faq.answer: Yes. It was redesigned as a park in 1905 and is a protected horticultural monument with clipped thuja trees and quiet paths. Visitors should stay respectful, since it is still an active cemetery.

faq.question: Is Varaždin expensive for couples?
faq.answer: No. Coffee costs about €2–3, a glass of local wine €3–5, and a main course roughly €8–15. A couple can manage on €120–180 per day, including a mid-range hotel, outside festival periods.

quickAnswer: Varaždin suits couples who want a walkable baroque town without crowds. Spend one evening on King Tomislav Square, walk the park-like Varaždin Cemetery, and add a day trip to Trakošćan Castle. Two nights is enough. The town lies 79 km north of Zagreb, and late May or September is the best time to go.
